question: What preset profiles can I pass to cacheLife?
expectedAnswer: cacheLife has preset profiles: default (used when none is given), seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks and max. Each sets stale, revalidate and expire times; for example default is 5 min stale, 15 min revalidate, never expire.

question: How do I label cached data so I can invalidate just that data later?
expectedAnswer: Call cacheTag('name') inside a 'use cache' function or component to tag its cached result, then invalidate it on demand with revalidateTag or updateTag.

question: How do I limit which paths my proxy file runs on?
expectedAnswer: Export a config object with a matcher from the proxy file. It accepts a path string, an array of paths, or patterns; without a matcher, proxy runs on every request including static assets.

question: How do I read an incoming request header like user-agent in a Server Component?
expectedAnswer: Import headers from 'next/headers', await headers() in the Server Component, and call .get('user-agent') on the result. headers() is async and read-only.

question: Where am I allowed to set or delete cookies, and how?
expectedAnswer: Cookies can only be set or deleted in a Server Function (Server Action) or a Route Handler, using (await cookies()).set(name, value, options) or .delete(name). Server Components can only read cookies.

alt.heading: cookies › Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Functions

question: If a page streams with loading.js, what HTTP status code does the response get?
expectedAnswer: Streaming responses start with a 200 status code. Redirects and not-found/forbidden/unauthorized responses that happen later are streamed rather than changing the initial status.

question: How do I show one custom 404 page for URLs that don't match any route at all?
expectedAnswer: Use the experimental global-not-found.js file. It renders for URLs that match no route and bypasses the normal layouts, so it must import its own global styles and fonts.

question: How do I prerender a page for every blog post slug at build time?
expectedAnswer: Export generateStaticParams from the dynamic route (e.g. app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx) and return an array of params objects such as { slug }; those routes are prerendered at build time.

question: How do I set the page title from data I fetch for that page?
expectedAnswer: Export an async generateMetadata function from the page or layout. It receives the route params, can fetch data, and returns a Metadata object with the title.

question: How do I allow next/image to load pictures from an external domain?
expectedAnswer: Add the external host to images.remotePatterns in next.config (as a URL or { protocol, hostname, port, pathname, search } objects), then pass the full URL as src with explicit width and height.

gold.heading: Image Component › Reference › Configuration options › remotePatterns

question: How do I keep the scroll position instead of jumping to the top when a Link navigates?
expectedAnswer: Pass scroll={false} to the Link (or scroll: false to router.push/replace). By default Link keeps the scroll position when the page stays visible and otherwise scrolls to the top of the new page.

gold.heading: Link Component › Examples › Disable scrolling to the top of the page

question: How do I read query string parameters in a Route Handler?
expectedAnswer: The Route Handler receives a NextRequest; read request.nextUrl.searchParams and call .get('name').

question: How can I run logging or analytics after the response has finished sending?
expectedAnswer: Use after() from 'next/server': pass it a callback and it runs once the response or prerender has finished. It works in Server Components, Server Functions, Route Handlers and Proxy.

question: What's the difference between redirect and permanentRedirect?
expectedAnswer: Both redirect to another URL and work in Server and Client Components, Route Handlers and Server Functions. redirect sends a 307 temporary redirect (303 for Server Actions), while permanentRedirect sends a 308 permanent redirect.

question: How do I let my headless CMS open a preview of unpublished content?
expectedAnswer: Create a Route Handler that calls (await draftMode()).enable(), which sets the __prerender_bypass cookie. Configure the CMS draft URL to call it with a secret token, verify the token and slug, then redirect to the content.

gold.heading: How to preview content with Draft Mode in Next.js › Step 1: Create a Route Handler
How to preview content with Draft Mode in Next.js › Step 2: Access the Route Handler from your headless CMS

question: How do I let one route run longer than the default function timeout?
expectedAnswer: Export maxDuration (seconds) from the route's page, layout or route file, e.g. export const maxDuration = 5. For Server Actions, set it at the page level.

question: My Server Action fails with large uploads. How do I raise the request body size limit?
expectedAnswer: Server Action request bodies are limited to 1MB by default. Raise it with serverActions.bodySizeLimit in next.config, using bytes or a string like '2mb'.

question: How do I send server errors to an observability service like Sentry?
expectedAnswer: Export an onRequestError function from instrumentation.ts. Next.js calls it with the error and request context whenever the server captures an error, so you can forward it to your provider; await any async work.

question: How do I make a component render at request time when it doesn't read cookies or headers?
expectedAnswer: Call await connection() from 'next/server' in the component. Prerendering stops there and the rest runs per request, which suits values like Math.random() or new Date().

question: How do I build a search box that puts the query in the URL and navigates without a full page reload?
expectedAnswer: Use the Form component from 'next/form' with a string action, e.g. <Form action="/search"><input name="query" /></Form>. On submit it appends the inputs to the URL as search params and navigates client-side, with prefetching of the loading UI.

question: How do I receive a webhook POST from a third-party service?
expectedAnswer: Create a Route Handler that exports a POST function, read the payload with request.text() or request.json(), and return a Response. No bodyParser configuration is needed.

question: Which kinds of values can't be passed as arguments to a function marked 'use cache'?
expectedAnswer: Arguments must be serializable with React Server Components serialization. Class instances, functions (except pass-through), symbols, WeakMaps, WeakSets and URL instances are not supported.

question: How do I cache data that depends on the user's cookies?
expectedAnswer: Plain 'use cache' can't read cookies or headers directly: read the values outside and pass them in as arguments so they become part of the cache key. Alternatively use 'use cache: private', which may call cookies() and headers() inside but is not stored in a server-side cache across requests.

question: After a Server Action saves data, how do I make the page show the new data right away?
expectedAnswer: Tag the cached data with cacheTag, then call updateTag(tag) in the Server Action after saving. It expires the entry immediately so the user sees their change, unlike revalidateTag's stale-while-revalidate behavior; updateTag works only in Server Actions.

question: How do I make sure only signed-in users can see certain pages and call certain actions?
expectedAnswer: Combine optimistic checks (session cookie in proxy, for redirects and UI) with secure checks against the session data close to the data: verify the session in a data access layer, in Server Components before rendering, and inside every Server Action and Route Handler.

gold.heading: How to implement authentication in Next.js › Authorization

question: I'm self-hosting several instances behind a load balancer. How should caching and revalidation be set up?
expectedAnswer: By default each instance caches on its own local disk, so configure a shared cache handler plus the same encryption key and deployment ID across instances. revalidateTag only affects the instance that calls it, so implement refreshTags in the custom cache handler to coordinate tag invalidation.

gold.heading: How to self-host your Next.js application › Caching and ISR
How to self-host your Next.js application › Multi-Instance Cache Coordination

question: How do I build a photo modal that has its own shareable URL but opens over the current page?
expectedAnswer: Combine parallel routes and intercepting routes: put the modal in a slot such as @modal, intercept the photo route there (e.g. (.)photo/[id]) to show it over the current page, and keep the normal photo route so a shared URL or refresh renders the full page. Add a default.js for the slot.

question: How do I show the rest of the page immediately while one slow part is still loading?
expectedAnswer: Stream the response: wrap the slow component in <Suspense> with a fallback, or add loading.js for a whole route segment. The fast parts are sent immediately and the slow part streams in when ready.

alt.heading: Fetching Data › Fetching data › Streaming › With loading.js

question: How do I expose an environment variable to browser code, and which .env file wins if a variable is defined twice?
expectedAnswer: Prefix the variable with NEXT_PUBLIC_ so its value is inlined into the client bundle at build time. Lookup order is process.env, .env.$(NODE_ENV).local, .env.local (not in test), .env.$(NODE_ENV), then .env; the first match wins.

gold.heading: How to use environment variables in Next.js › Bundling Environment Variables for the Browser
How to use environment variables in Next.js › Environment Variable Load Order

question: How do I serve /en and /fr versions of my pages and still prerender them statically?
expectedAnswer: Put routes under a dynamic [lang] segment, pick the locale from the Accept-Language header in proxy and redirect to the localized path, and export generateStaticParams returning each locale from the [lang] layout to prerender them.

question: How do I refresh cached content every hour and also immediately when an editor publishes a change?
expectedAnswer: Use both: a cacheLife profile (e.g. 'hours') for time-based refresh, plus cacheTag on the data and revalidateTag (or updateTag from a Server Action) when an editor publishes. The two approaches are designed to be combined.

question: How should I handle expected errors like failed form validation versus unexpected exceptions?
expectedAnswer: Expected errors such as validation failures should be returned as values (e.g. from a Server Action via useActionState) and shown in the UI, not thrown. Unexpected exceptions are caught by error boundaries defined with error.js, which can offer a retry().

question: How do cached content and Suspense combine on a page that has both static and personalized parts?
expectedAnswer: Cached content ('use cache') and static parts go into the prerendered static shell. Request-specific parts wrapped in <Suspense> contribute their fallback to the shell and stream in at request time, so one page mixes static, cached and streamed content.

question: When my CMS calls a webhook, how do I clear the cached pages that show that content?
expectedAnswer: Add a Route Handler that receives the CMS webhook (POST) and calls revalidateTag(tag, 'max') for the tags used on the affected cached data. revalidateTag works in Route Handlers and Server Functions but not in Client Components or Proxy.

question: How can I show a fallback for one failing Server Component without adding an error.js file?
expectedAnswer: Use catchError from 'next/error' to create an error-boundary component with a fallback, then wrap the risky part of the tree with it. It is a programmatic alternative to error.js and supports retry().

question: What is io() for, and how is it different from connection()?
expectedAnswer: With Cache Components, await io() keeps a synchronous value like new Date() or Math.random() out of the static shell by suspending during prerender; it resolves immediately at request time and in cached scopes. connection() instead marks rendering as waiting for an incoming request.

question: How can a deeply nested component read the [lang] segment of my root layout without passing props down?
expectedAnswer: Import the getter for the root segment from 'next/root-params' (e.g. import { lang } from 'next/root-params') and await lang() in any Server Component. The export names come from the root layout's dynamic segment names.

question: What does setting ensureStatic to 'shell' check?
expectedAnswer: ensureStatic = 'shell' requires the App Shell loaded by a default <Link> prefetch to be static. It needs Partial Prefetching; without it there is no App Shell, the setting has no effect and Next.js logs a warning.

question: How do I test that navigating to a route stays instant?
expectedAnswer: Use the instant() helper from @next/playwright in an end-to-end test; it holds back dynamic content while the callback asserts on the instant UI. It is available in development, and production builds need experimental.exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild.

alt.heading: Ensuring instant navigations › Prevent regressions with e2e tests

question: How do I turn off prefetching for a whole route segment rather than one Link?
expectedAnswer: Export prefetch = 'force-disabled' from the segment's layout or page. The prefetch segment config requires cacheComponents and can't be used in a Client Component segment.

question: When should I call navigation() instead of connection()?
expectedAnswer: Call await navigation() to keep expensive but reusable work out of the App Shell and per-link prefetches: it runs when the user navigates while the nearest Suspense fallback is prefetched, and static prerenders still include the content. connection() instead makes the work request-time.

question: How do I stop next dev from writing a managed block into my AGENTS.md file?
expectedAnswer: Set agentRules: false in next.config. The next next dev run removes the managed block and stops updating it; create-next-app's --no-agents-md flag avoids creating the file in new projects.

question: In error.js, how do I try rendering the segment again after an error?
expectedAnswer: Call the retry() function passed to the error component (e.g. from a 'Try again' button). It re-fetches and re-renders the boundary's children and replaces the fallback if that succeeds.

question: How do I write the bundle analyzer output to files instead of opening the interactive view?
expectedAnswer: Run next analyze export: it streams an existing analysis snapshot as JSON Lines without starting the web UI, with options such as the app directory and --snapshot to pick a snapshot.

gold.heading: next CLI › Reference › next analyze export options

question: Is middleware.ts still the right file name in Next.js 16?
expectedAnswer: No. In Next.js 16 middleware is deprecated and renamed to proxy: rename middleware.ts to proxy.ts and the exported function to proxy. Proxy runs on the Node.js runtime only, so keep middleware if you need the edge runtime.

gold.heading: How to upgrade to version 16 › middleware to proxy

question: Can I still read params and searchParams synchronously in version 16?
expectedAnswer: No. Next.js 16 removes the temporary synchronous access, so params, searchParams, cookies, headers and draftMode must be awaited.

gold.heading: How to upgrade to version 16 › Async Request APIs (Breaking change)

question: Does next build use Turbopack by default now, and how do I go back to webpack?
expectedAnswer: Yes. Since Next.js 16, Turbopack is the default for both next dev and next build, so --turbopack flags are unnecessary; projects that need webpack (e.g. a custom webpack config) can opt out with the --webpack flag.

gold.heading: How to upgrade to version 16 › Turbopack by default

question: What should replace export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' after enabling Cache Components?
expectedAnswer: Remove it. With Cache Components, uncached data and request-time APIs already run at request time and Next.js prerenders static or cached UI around them; then follow any validation errors.

question: Should I keep using unstable_cache with Cache Components?
expectedAnswer: It keeps working, so no change is required. To migrate later, turn the wrapped function into a 'use cache' function, drop the key parts (keys come from the arguments) and map options to cacheLife and cacheTag.

question: What happened to the experimental_ppr route option?
expectedAnswer: Next.js 16 removed experimental.ppr and the experimental_ppr segment config. Partial Prerendering is now part of Cache Components: enable cacheComponents and remove the old flags (a codemod handles the segment config).

gold.heading: How to upgrade to version 16 › Partial Prerendering (PPR)

question: Do parallel route slots need a default.js file in version 16?
expectedAnswer: Yes. All parallel route slots now need an explicit default.js or builds fail; to keep the old behavior, have it call notFound() or return null.

gold.heading: How to upgrade to version 16 › Parallel Routes default.js requirement

question: What is the minimum Node.js version for Next.js 16?
expectedAnswer: Node.js 20.9.0 (LTS); Node.js 18 is no longer supported. TypeScript 5.1+ is also required.

gold.heading: How to upgrade to version 16 › Node.js runtime and browser support
